chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Joe Smith and Louis Armstrong on those records
summary: Prompted by Dance, Thomas names Joe Smith and Louis Armstrong ("Pops") as the trumpeters he heard on blues records.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But, also I mean what I really meant was on records like Bessie Smith and Nomie Smith, etc., I mean they would be having these people like Joe Smith, Louis Armstrong, probably too.

Well, let me tell you about that. That's another part of the story. That's the reason I don't want to leave Webster Groves, you know. And, Joe Smith, beautiful trumpet player, you know, as you know .... And, Pops, always called Louis Armstrong, he was tremendous. And I think possibly the greatest horn (?) I've heard and a great guy. And ... I've got some funny stories to tell about Pops.
Well, we're going to come to that.
Now I've still got to get to Jeff City, huh?
What you're really talking about is what you'd heard before you left Webster Groves.
